249	\subsection{Smoothing, noise and the estimator}
250	
251	\paragraph{Resolution and smoother.} Let $J:=\lfloor\log_2n/(2\alpha+d+3)\rfloor$. Then
252	\begin{equation}\label{eq:J}
253	n^{-1/2}\le2^{-J(\alpha+(d+3)/2)},\qquad n^{-1}2^{J(d+3)}\le2^{-2J\alpha},\qquad 2^{-2J\alpha}\le 2^{2\alpha}\rate,\qquad J\le\log_2n .
254	\end{equation}
255	Put $K_Jg:=(k_J*Eg)|_D$, with $k_J$ from (C2) and $E$ from (C1). On data, $K_JY(x)=\langle Y,k_J(x,\cdot)\rangle$, where $k_J(x,\cdot):=E^*[k_J(x-\cdot)]\in L^2(D)$; this is defined for all $x\in\R^d$. By the change of variables $z=R_it$, $E^*$ is the identity on $D$ plus finitely many terms of the form $a_i(\chi\varphi)(R_i^{-1}z)|\det DR_i^{-1}(z)|$. These are supported on shells $\{1-\lambda_i\eta<|z|<1\}$ and have bounded Jacobians. This gives the following kernel bounds.
256	\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=3.2em]
257	\item[\textbf{(K1)}] $|\partial^\iota_xk_J(x,z)|\le C2^{J(d+|\iota|)}$ for $|\iota|\le4$.
258	\item[\textbf{(K2)}] $\partial^\iota_xk_J(x,z)=0$ unless $|x-z|\le C_02^{-J}$. Indeed, for the reflected terms let $t=R_i^{-1}z$, so $|t|>1$. If $x\in D$ and $|x-t|\le C2^{-J}$, then $|t|-1\le C2^{-J}$ and $|z-t|=(1+\lambda_i)(|t|-1)\le C2^{-J}$.
259	\item[\textbf{(K3)}] $\|\partial^\iota_xk_J(x,\cdot)\|^2_2\le C2^{J(d+2|\iota|)}$, and $x\mapsto\partial_x^\iota k_J(x,\cdot)$ is Lipschitz into $L^2$ with constant $C2^{J(d/2+|\iota|+1)}$, for $|\iota|\le3$. This follows from (K1), (K2) and the fact that the support in $z$ has volume $\le C2^{-Jd}$.
260	\end{enumerate}
261	
262	\paragraph{Notation.} Let $U=Eu$, $F=Ef$, $V=\nabla u$ and $V^E=\nabla U$. By (C1) and \eqref{eq:C4}, $\|F\|_{C^\alpha}+\|V^E\|_{C^\alpha}\le C$. Let
263	\[
264	V_J:=\nabla K_Ju=(k_J*V^E)|_D,\qquad e:=K_Ju-u,\qquad \xi:=n^{-1/2}K_J\W,\qquad\hat V:=\nabla K_JY=V_J+\nabla\xi .
265	\]
266	$V_J$ is the restriction of a $C^\infty$ field on $\R^d$. By (G) and (K1)--(K3), $\xi$ is a centred Gaussian field with $C^3$ sample paths on a neighbourhood of $D$ (it is in fact smooth), and $\xi$ does not depend on $f$.
267	
268	\paragraph{Good event.} Let
269	\[
270	\cA:=\Big\{\max_{|\iota|=m}\sup_D|\partial^\iota\xi|\le Jn^{-1/2}2^{J(d/2+m)},\ m=1,2,3\Big\}.
271	\]
272	On $\cA$, by \eqref{eq:J} and after adjusting constants for operator norms,
273	\begin{equation}\label{eq:xi}
274	\|\nabla\xi\|_\infty\le CJ2^{-J(\alpha+1/2)},\qquad\|D^2\xi\|_\infty\le CJ2^{-J(\alpha-1/2)},\qquad\|D^3\xi\|_\infty\le CJ2^{-J(\alpha-3/2)} .
275	\end{equation}
276	
277	\begin{definition}[Estimator]\label{def:est}
278	Let $\varepsilon_0:=1/(8d)$, and define the observable event $\cB:=\{\|\hat V-x/d\|_{C^1(D)}\le\varepsilon_0\}$. On $\cB$ set $\hat f:=T^{-1}_{\hat V}\one$ (Definition~\ref{def:T}); off $\cB$ set $\hat f:=\one$. Let $\tilde f:=\min(\max(\hat f,1-r),1+r)$.
279	\end{definition}
280	
281	Since $\|f-1\|_\infty\le r$, clipping can only decrease $|\tilde f-f|$ pointwise. The estimator uses only $Y$, $n$, $\alpha$, $r$ and the fixed kernels. The event $\cA$ itself is not observable: $\xi$ does not depend on $f$, but $\xi=K_JY-K_Ju$ cannot be computed from the data because $u$ is unknown. 285	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:LP}
286	Let $g\in C^s(\R^d)$, $s>0$, and let $m\ge1$ be an integer. Then $\|D^m(k_J*g)\|_\infty$ is at most $C2^{J(m-s)}\|g\|_{C^s}$ if $m>s$, at most $C(J+1)\|g\|_{C^s}$ if $m=s$, and at most $C\|g\|_{C^s}$ if $m<s$.

290	By (LP), $D^m(k_J*g)=\sum_j(D^mk_J)*\Delta_jg$, and the series converges uniformly because each term is $\le\|D^mk_J\|_1\|\Delta_jg\|_\infty\le C2^{Jm}2^{-js}\|g\|_{C^s}$. For $j\le J$, write the term as $k_J*D^m\Delta_jg$; by Bernstein it is $\le C2^{j(m-s)}\|g\|_{C^s}$. For $j>J$, the first bound gives $C2^{Jm-js}\|g\|_{C^s}$, and summing over $j>J$ gives $C2^{J(m-s)}\|g\|_{C^s}$. Summing the bound $C2^{j(m-s)}$ over $j\le J$ gives the three cases.
291	\end{proof}

294	Let $\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$. There are $r_0$ and $J_0$ such that for $r\le r_0$ and $J\ge J_0$:

306	\subsection{Geometry of the flow and the transport inverse}
307	
308	\paragraph{Setting.} Let $X$ be the restriction to $D$ of a $C^k$ field ($k\ge1$) on a neighbourhood of $D$, with
309	\[
310	\|X-x/d\|_{C^1(D)}:=\max\big(\sup_D|X-x/d|,\ \sup_D\|DX-I/d\|\big)\le\varepsilon\le1/(8d).
311	\]
312	Put $\nu:=1/d-\varepsilon\ge7/(8d)$. Let $\Phi_t$ be the flow of $X$, let $\gamma(s)=\gamma_x(s)=\Phi_{-s}x$ be the backward ray from $x$, and let
313	\[
314	w(s,x):=\exp\Big(-\int_0^s\dv X(\Phi_{-\sigma}x)\,d\sigma\Big).
315	\]
316	
317	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:geom}
318	In this setting the following hold.
319	\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
320	\item $X$ has exactly one zero $x_X\in D$, and $|x_X|\le d\varepsilon$.
321	\item With $\rho(y)=|y-x_X|$: $(y-x_X)\cdot X(y)\ge(1/d-\varepsilon)\rho^2$ and $|X(y)|\le(1/d+\varepsilon)\rho$ on $D$.
322	\item For $x\in D$, $\Phi_{-s}x$ exists for all $s\ge0$ and stays in $D$. It lies in $\Dint$ for $s>0$, and $\Dint$ is invariant.
323	\item $\varrho(s):=\rho(\gamma(s))$ satisfies $\varrho(0)e^{-(1/d+\varepsilon)s}\le\varrho(s)\le\varrho(0)e^{-(1/d-\varepsilon)s}$. If $\varrho(0)>0$, then $-(1/d+\varepsilon)\varrho\le\varrho'\le-\nu\varrho$.
324	\item The propagator $P(s,\sigma)$ of $y'=-DX(\gamma)y$ satisfies $\|P(s,\sigma)\|\le e^{-\nu(s-\sigma)}$. In particular $\|D\Phi_{-s}\|\le e^{-\nu s}$.
325	\item $1-d\varepsilon\le\dv X\le1+d\varepsilon$, so $e^{-(1+d\varepsilon)s}\le w\le e^{-(1-d\varepsilon)s}\le e^{-7s/8}$.
326	\end{enumerate}
327	\end{lemma}
328	
329	\begin{proof}
330	(1) The map $x\mapsto x-dX(x)=-d(X-x/d)$ sends $D$ into $B(0,d\varepsilon)\subset D$ and is a $d\varepsilon$-contraction on the convex set $D$. Its unique fixed point is the unique zero of $X$.
331	(2) $X(y)=Q(y)(y-x_X)$ with $Q=\int_0^1DX(x_X+t(y-x_X))\,dt$ and $\|Q-I/d\|\le\varepsilon$; the segment lies in $D$ by convexity.
332	(3) For $|z|=1$, $z\cdot X(z)\ge1/d-\varepsilon>0$, so $\frac{d}{ds}|\gamma|^2=-2\gamma\cdot X(\gamma)<0$ whenever $|\gamma|=1$. A first-exit-time argument gives invariance of $D$ and of $\Dint$, and shows that boundary points enter $\Dint$ immediately. Global existence holds because $D$ is compact.
333	(4) $(\varrho^2)'=-2(\gamma-x_X)\cdot X(\gamma)$; apply (2) and Gronwall's inequality.
334	(5) $v\cdot DX\,v\ge\nu|v|^2$ on $D$, so $(|y|^2)'\le-2\nu|y|^2$. Also $D\Phi_{-s}=P(s,0)$.
335	(6) $\dv X=1+\operatorname{tr}(DX-I/d)$ and $|\operatorname{tr}A|\le d\|A\|$.
336	\end{proof}
337	
338	\begin{definition}\label{def:T}
339	For $g\in C^1(D)$ put $T_Xg:=\dv(gX)$. For $H\in C(D)$ put
340	\[
341	T_X^{-1}H(x):=\int_0^\infty H(\Phi_{-s}x)\,w(s,x)\,ds .
342	\]
343	By Lemma~\ref{lem:geom}(6) the integral converges absolutely and uniformly, and $T^{-1}_XH\in C(D)$.
344	\end{definition}
345	
346	Since $w(s,\Phi_{-t}x)=w(s+t,x)/w(t,x)$, we have the semigroup identity
347	\begin{equation}\label{eq:SG}
348	w(t,x)\,T^{-1}_XH(\Phi_{-t}x)=\int_t^\infty H(\Phi_{-s}x)\,w(s,x)\,ds .
349	\end{equation}
350	
351	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:T}
352	In the setting of Lemma~\ref{lem:geom}:
353	\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
354	\item[\textup{(a)}] \textup{(Uniqueness.)} If $g\in C^1(D)$ and $\dv(gX)=H$ on $\Dint$ with $H\in C(D)$, then $g=T^{-1}_XH$.
355	\item[\textup{(a$'$)}] \textup{(Right inverse.)} If $H\in C(D)$ and $g:=T^{-1}_XH\in C^1(D)$, then $\dv(gX)=H$ on $D$.
356	\item[\textup{(b)}] $\|T^{-1}_XH\|_\infty\le\frac87\|H\|_\infty\le2\|H\|_\infty$.
357	\item[\textup{(c)}] \textup{(Boundary layer.)} If $H=0$ on $\{|x|\le1-\delta\}$, then $\|T^{-1}_XH\|_\infty\le6d\delta\|H\|_\infty$.
358	\end{enumerate}
359	\end{lemma}
360	
361	\begin{proof}
362	(a) Fix $x\in D$. For $s>0$, $\gamma(s)\in\Dint$, and $\psi(s)=g(\gamma(s))w(s,x)$ satisfies
363	$\psi'=-(X\cdot\nabla g+g\dv X)(\gamma)\,w=-H(\gamma)\,w$.
364	Integrate over $[\delta,S]$, then let $\delta\to0$ (by continuity) and $S\to\infty$ (using $|\psi(S)|\le\|g\|_\infty e^{-7S/8}$). This gives $g(x)=\int_0^\infty H(\gamma(s))w(s,x)\,ds$.
365	
366	(a$'$) Fix $x\in\Dint$ and differentiate \eqref{eq:SG} at $t=0^+$. The right side gives $-H(x)$. Since $w(0,x)=1$ and $\partial_tw(0,x)=-\dv X(x)$, the left side gives $-\nabla g(x)\cdot X(x)-g(x)\dv X(x)$. Extend to $D$ by continuity.
367	
368	(b) Use $w\le e^{-7s/8}$.
369	
370	(c) The case $\delta>1/2$ follows from (b), since then $6d\delta>2$. Let $\delta\le1/2$ and $\phi=|\gamma|^2$. Where $|\gamma|\ge1/2$, $\gamma\cdot X(\gamma)\ge|\gamma|(|\gamma|/d-\varepsilon)\ge3/(16d)$, so $\phi'\le-3/(8d)$. Hence $\phi$ drops below $(1-\delta)^2$ within time $\le(1-(1-\delta)^2)\cdot8d/3\le6d\delta$, and by the same sign argument it never returns. Since $H(\gamma(s))=0$ afterwards and $w\le1$, the claim follows.
371	\end{proof}
372	
373	\begin{lemma}[Flow derivatives, uniform in $s$]\label{lem:flowder}
374	Let $M=D\Phi_{-s}$, $N=D^2\Phi_{-s}$ and $\ell=\log w$, all differentiated in $x$.
375	\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
376	\item If $X\in C^2$: $\|N(s)\|\le\|D^2X\|_\infty e^{-\nu s}/\nu$ and $|D_x\ell|\le\|D\dv X\|_\infty/\nu$.
377	\item If $X\in C^3$: $\|D_x^2\ell\|\le\|D^2\dv X\|_\infty/(2\nu)+\|D\dv X\|_\infty\|D^2X\|_\infty/\nu^2$.
378	\end{enumerate}
379	\end{lemma}
380	
381	\begin{proof}
382	$N$ solves $N'=-DX(\gamma)N-D^2X(\gamma)[M\cdot,M\cdot]$ with $N(0)=0$. By Duhamel's formula and Lemma~\ref{lem:geom}(5),
383	$\|N(s)\|\le\int_0^se^{-\nu(s-\sigma)}\|D^2X\|_\infty e^{-2\nu\sigma}d\sigma\le\|D^2X\|_\infty e^{-\nu s}/\nu$.
384	Next, $D_x\ell[v]=-\int_0^sD\dv X(\gamma)[Mv]\,d\sigma$, and $\int_0^\infty e^{-\nu\sigma}d\sigma=1/\nu$. Finally,
385	$D^2_x\ell[v,v']=-\int_0^s\big(D^2\dv X(\gamma)[Mv,Mv']+D\dv X(\gamma)[N[v,v']]\big)d\sigma$; bound this with the two previous estimates.
386	\end{proof}
387	
388	\paragraph{Differentiation under the integral.} Let the integrand be $H(\Phi_{-s}x)w(s,x)$ or $w(s,x)$. By (ODE), and since the flow is defined on a neighbourhood of $D$, its $x$-derivatives up to the relevant order are jointly continuous on $[0,\infty)\times D$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:flowder} and the identities $D_xw=w\,D_x\ell$ and $D_x^2w=w(D_x^2\ell+D_x\ell\otimes D_x\ell)$, they are dominated by $Ke^{-7s/8}$. Truncating the integral at $S$, differentiating, and passing to the uniform limit gives the following.
389	
390	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:Treg}
391	All constants below depend only on $d$, uniformly over $\|X-x/d\|_{C^1}\le\varepsilon\le1/(8d)$.
392	\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
393	\item[\textup{(d)}] If $X\in C^2$ and $H\in C^1(D)$, then $T^{-1}_XH\in C^1(D)$ and
394	$\|\nabla T^{-1}_XH\|_\infty\le C_d(\|\nabla H\|_\infty+\|H\|_\infty\|D\dv X\|_\infty)$.
395	\item[\textup{(e)}] If $X\in C^3$, then $T^{-1}_X\one\in C^2(D)$, $\|\nabla T^{-1}_X\one\|_\infty\le C_d\|D\dv X\|_\infty$, and
396	$\|D^2T_X^{-1}\one\|_\infty\le C_d\big(\|D^2\dv X\|_\infty+\|D\dv X\|_\infty^2+\|D\dv X\|_\infty\|D^2X\|_\infty\big)$.
397	\end{enumerate}
398	\end{lemma}
399	
400	\subsection{The centring function and an exact decomposition}
401	
402	Fix $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:fields}, so that Lemmas~\ref{lem:geom}--\ref{lem:Treg} apply to $X=V_J$ (with $\varepsilon_0/2$), and on $\cA$ also to $X=\hat V$. Let
403	\[
404	\bar f:=T^{-1}_{V_J}\one .
405	\]
406	Using $\|D^m\dv V_J\|_\infty\le d\|D^{m+1}V_J\|_\infty$, Lemma~\ref{lem:fields}(3) and Lemma~\ref{lem:Treg}(e),
407	\begin{equation}\label{eq:fbar}
408	\|\bar f\|_\infty\le2,\qquad\|\nabla\bar f\|_\infty\le CJ2^{J(2-\alpha)_+},\qquad\|D^2\bar f\|_\infty\le CJ^22^{J(3-\alpha)_+} .
409	\end{equation}
410	The last bound uses $2(2-\alpha)_+\le(3-\alpha)_+$ for $\alpha\ge1$. Moreover $\bar f\in C^2(D)$, and $\dv(\bar fV_J)=1$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(a$'$).
411	
412	\paragraph{Noise term.} Let $G_\xi:=\dv(\bar f\nabla\xi)=\bar f\Delta\xi+\nabla\bar f\cdot\nabla\xi\in C^1(D)$ and $Z:=T^{-1}_{V_J}G_\xi$. Since $V_J$ is deterministic, $Z$ is defined for every realisation. By Lemma~\ref{lem:Treg}(d), $Z\in C^1(D)$, and $T_{V_J}Z=G_\xi$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(a$'$).
413	
414	\begin{proposition}\label{prop:star}
415	On $\cA$ (so that $\hat V$ satisfies the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:geom} and $\hat f=T^{-1}_{\hat V}\one$),
416	\begin{equation}\label{eq:star}
417	\hat f-f=(\bar f-f)-Z+T^{-1}_{\hat V}\dv(Z\nabla\xi).
418	\end{equation}
419	\end{proposition}
420	
421	\begin{proof}
422	$\hat V$ is $C^3$ on a neighbourhood of $D$, so $\hat f\in C^2$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:Treg}(e), and $T_{\hat V}\hat f=1$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(a$'$). Hence
423	$T_{\hat V}(\hat f-\bar f)=1-\dv(\bar fV_J)-\dv(\bar f\nabla\xi)=-G_\xi$.
424	Also $T_{\hat V}Z=T_{V_J}Z+\dv(Z\nabla\xi)=G_\xi+\dv(Z\nabla\xi)$. Therefore $T_{\hat V}(\hat f-\bar f+Z)=\dv(Z\nabla\xi)$, which is continuous. Since $\hat f-\bar f+Z\in C^1$, Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(a) with $X=\hat V$ gives $\hat f-\bar f+Z=T^{-1}_{\hat V}\dv(Z\nabla\xi)$, which is \eqref{eq:star}.
425	\end{proof}
426	
427	\subsection{\texorpdfstring{The bias: $\|\bar f-f\|_\infty\le CJ^22^{-J\alpha}$}{The bias}}
428	
429	\begin{proposition}\label{prop:bias}
430	Uniformly over $f\in\Fc(\alpha,r)$, $\|\bar f-f\|_\infty\le CJ^22^{-J\alpha}$, with no factor $J^2$ when $\alpha\notin\mathbb N$.
431	\end{proposition}
432	
433	\begin{proof}
434	\emph{Reduction.} $f\in C^1$ (as $\alpha>1$), $u\in C^{\alpha+1}\subset C^2$ by \eqref{eq:C4}, $\dv(fV)=1$, and $V_J-V=\nabla e$ on $D$. So
435	$T_{V_J}(\bar f-f)=1-\dv(fV_J)=-\dv(f\nabla e)$, and by Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(a), $\bar f-f=-T^{-1}_{V_J}\dv(f\nabla e)$.
436	
437	\emph{Commutator.} Let $g:=F-k_J*F$ and $R(x):=-\int k_J(-h)\Delta_hF(x)\Delta_hV^E(x)\,dh$. Then
438	\[
439	F\,(k_J*V^E)=k_J*(FV^E)+gV^E+R .
440	\]
441	Indeed, $F(x)(k_J*V^E)(x)-k_J*(FV^E)(x)=\int k_J(y)[F(x)-F(x-y)]V^E(x-y)\,dy$. Insert $F(x)-F(x-y)=-\Delta_{-y}F(x)$ and $V^E(x-y)=V^E(x)+\Delta_{-y}V^E(x)$, and use $\int k_J=1$; the first part gives $gV^E$ and the second, after $h=-y$, gives $R$. Let $\Gamma:=\dv(FV^E)-1$, which lies in $C^{\alpha-1}(\R^d)$ by the algebra property and vanishes on $D$. Since $\dv(k_J*(FV^E))=k_J*\Gamma+1$, on $D$
442	\[
443	\dv(f\nabla e)=\dv(fV_J)-1=k_J*\Gamma+\dv(gV)+\dv R .
444	\]
445	We treat the three terms in turn, using linearity of $T^{-1}_{V_J}$.
446	
447	\emph{(i) The term $\dv(gV)$.} Since $V=V_J-\nabla e$, we have $\dv(gV)=T_{V_J}g-\dv(g\nabla e)$. As $g\in C^1$, Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(a) gives $T^{-1}_{V_J}\dv(gV)=g-T^{-1}_{V_J}\dv(g\nabla e)$. By (C2) (applied to $F\in C^\alpha$ and $U\in C^{\alpha+1}$): $\|g\|_\infty\le C2^{-J\alpha}$, $\|\nabla g\|_\infty\le C2^{-J(\alpha-1)}$, $\|\nabla e\|_\infty\le C2^{-J\alpha}$ and $\|D^2e\|_\infty\le C2^{-J(\alpha-1)}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b), the contribution is $\le C2^{-J\alpha}+C2^{-J(2\alpha-1)}$.
448	
449	\emph{(ii) The term $\dv R$.} We have
450	$\partial R=-\int k_J(-h)\big[\Delta_h\partial F\,\Delta_hV^E+\Delta_hF\,\Delta_h\partial V^E\big]dh$.
451	Each product has the form $\Delta_h\phi_1\,\Delta_h\phi_2$ with $\phi_i\in C^{s_i}$ and $(s_1,s_2)=(\alpha-1,\alpha)$ or $(\alpha,\alpha-1)$. By (C3), and using $|P_{\phi_i}|\le C|h|$ for $|h|\le1$, the product equals a polynomial in $h$ (with coefficients depending on $x$) whose monomials have degrees in $[2,s_1+s_2)=[2,2\alpha-1)$. The remainder is bounded by
452	$C|h|^{\min(1+s_1,\,1+s_2,\,s_1+s_2)}\Lambda(h)^2=C|h|^\alpha\Lambda(h)^2$.

462	\subsection{\texorpdfstring{The variance: $\E\|Z\|^2_2\le Cn^{-1}2^{J(d+3)}\le C2^{-2J\alpha}$}{The variance}}
463	
464	\begin{proposition}\label{prop:var}
465	$\E\|Z\|^2_{L^2(D)}\le Cn^{-1}2^{J(d+3)}\le C2^{-2J\alpha}$.
466	\end{proposition}
467	
468	\begin{proof}
469	\emph{Representation.} Let $\mathcal D_y:=\bar f(y)\Delta_y+\nabla\bar f(y)\cdot\nabla_y$. By (G), $G_\xi(y)=n^{-1/2}\W(\mathcal D_yk_J(y,\cdot))$, and since Bochner integrals commute with $\W$,
470	\[
471	Z(x)=n^{-1/2}\W(h_x),\qquad h_x=\int_0^\infty w(s,x)\,\mathcal D_yk_J(y,\cdot)\big|_{y=\gamma_x(s)}\,ds,
472	\]
473	where $\gamma_x$ is the backward ray of $V_J$. Hence $\E Z(x)^2=n^{-1}\|h_x\|_2^2$.
474	
475	\emph{Kernel bound.} Since $(2-\alpha)_+<1$, \eqref{eq:fbar} gives $\|\nabla\bar f\|_\infty\le CJ2^{J(2-\alpha)_+}\le C2^J$. With (K1) and (K2), $|\mathcal D_yk_J(y,z)|\le C2^{J(d+2)}\one\{|y-z|\le\delta_J\}$, where $\delta_J:=C_02^{-J}$. Let $\mu_x:=\int_0^\infty w(s,x)\,\delta_{\gamma_x(s)}\,ds$, a measure on $D$ of mass $\le 8/7$. Then
476	\[
477	|h_x(z)|\le C2^{J(d+2)}\mu_x(B(z,\delta_J)),\qquad
478	\|h_x\|_2^2\le C2^{2J(d+2)}\!\int\mu_x(B(z,\delta_J))^2dz\le C2^{2J(d+2)}\delta_J^d\!\int\mu_x(B(y,2\delta_J))\,\mu_x(dy).
479	\]
480	The last step is Fubini: $\int\mu(B(z,\delta))^2dz=\iint|B(y,\delta)\cap B(y',\delta)|\,\mu(dy)\mu(dy')$, and the intersection is empty unless $|y-y'|\le2\delta$.
481	
482	\emph{Ray measure.} Let $x_J$ be the zero of $V_J$, $\rho=|\cdot-x_J|$, and $\rho_x=\rho(x)>0$. Let $\varrho(s)=\rho(\gamma_x(s))$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:geom}(4),(6), $w(s,x)\le(\varrho(s)/\rho_x)^\beta$ with $\beta=d(1-d\varepsilon)/(1+d\varepsilon)\ge7d/9>1$. Moreover $\varrho$ decreases strictly from $\rho_x$ to $0$, with $|\varrho'|\ge\nu\varrho$. Changing variables $t=\varrho(s)$, for every $\varphi\ge0$,
483	\begin{equation}\label{eq:M}
484	\int\varphi\,d\mu_x\le\frac1\nu\int_0^{\rho_x}\varphi(\gamma_x\text{ at radius }t)\,(t/\rho_x)^\beta\,\frac{dt}{t}.
485	\end{equation}
486	
487	\emph{Small-ball mass.} If $|\gamma_x(s)-y|\le2\delta_J$, then $|\varrho(s)-\rho(y)|\le2\delta_J$. Hence, by \eqref{eq:M}, $m(y):=\mu_x(B(y,2\delta_J))$ satisfies
488	\[
489	m(y)\le C\delta_J\rho(y)^{\beta-1}\rho_x^{-\beta}\ \text{ if }\rho(y)\ge4\delta_J,\qquad m(y)\le C\min(1,\delta_J/\rho_x)^\beta\ \text{ if }\rho(y)<4\delta_J .
490	\]
491	(In the first case $t\in[\rho(y)/2,3\rho(y)/2]$ ranges over an interval of length $4\delta_J$; in the second $t\le\min(6\delta_J,\rho_x)$.)
492	
493	\emph{Integration.} Apply \eqref{eq:M} once more, with $\varphi=m$. The part with $t\ge4\delta_J$ is
494	$\le C\delta_J\rho_x^{-2\beta}\int_0^{\rho_x}t^{2\beta-2}dt\le C\delta_J/\rho_x$, since $2\beta-1>0$.
495	The part with $t<4\delta_J$ is $\le C\min(1,\delta_J/\rho_x)^{2\beta}\le C\min(1,\delta_J/\rho_x)$. Trivially, $\int m\,d\mu_x\le\mu_x(D)^2\le4$. Hence $\int m\,d\mu_x\le C\min(1,\delta_J/\rho_x)$, and
496	\[
497	\|h_x\|_2^2\le C2^{J(d+4)}\min(1,2^{-J}/\rho_x)\le C2^{J(d+3)}|x-x_J|^{-1}.
498	\]
499	Since $\int_D|x-x_J|^{-1}dx\le C$ for $d\ge2$, Tonelli's theorem and \eqref{eq:J} give $\E\|Z\|_2^2\le Cn^{-1}2^{J(d+3)}\le C2^{-2J\alpha}$.
500	\end{proof}

502	\subsection{The remainder and the bad event}
503	
504	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:rem}
505	On $\cA$, $\|T^{-1}_{\hat V}\dv(Z\nabla\xi)\|_\infty\le CJ^42^{-J(2\alpha-1)}$. This is $o(2^{-J\alpha})$ because $\alpha>1$.
506	\end{lemma}
507	
508	\begin{proof}
509	We use \eqref{eq:xi}, \eqref{eq:fbar}, $(2-\alpha)_+<1$ and $(3-\alpha)_+\le2$. First,
510	\[
511	\|G_\xi\|_\infty\le\|\bar f\|_\infty\|\Delta\xi\|_\infty+\|\nabla\bar f\|_\infty\|\nabla\xi\|_\infty\le CJ2^{-J(\alpha-1/2)}+CJ^22^{J(2-\alpha)_+-J(\alpha+1/2)}\le CJ^22^{-J(\alpha-1/2)} .
512	\]
513	Next, $\|\nabla G_\xi\|_\infty\le C(\|D^3\xi\|_\infty+\|\nabla\bar f\|_\infty\|D^2\xi\|_\infty+\|D^2\bar f\|_\infty\|\nabla\xi\|_\infty)\le CJ^32^{-J(\alpha-3/2)}$. Here each cross term has exponent $\le-(\alpha-3/2)$ because $\alpha\ge1$.
514	
515	By Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b) and Lemma~\ref{lem:Treg}(d), with $\|D\dv V_J\|_\infty\le d\|D^2V_J\|_\infty\le CJ2^{J(2-\alpha)_+}$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:fields}(3), we get
516	$\|Z\|_\infty\le CJ^22^{-J(\alpha-1/2)}$ and
517	$\|\nabla Z\|_\infty\le C(\|\nabla G_\xi\|_\infty+\|G_\xi\|_\infty J2^{J(2-\alpha)_+})\le CJ^32^{-J(\alpha-3/2)}$.
518	Hence
519	\[
520	\|\dv(Z\nabla\xi)\|_\infty\le\|\nabla Z\|_\infty\|\nabla\xi\|_\infty+\|Z\|_\infty\|\Delta\xi\|_\infty\le CJ^42^{-J(2\alpha-1)}+CJ^32^{-J(2\alpha-1)}\le CJ^42^{-J(2\alpha-1)} .
521	\]
522	Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b) for $X=\hat V$ concludes the proof.
523	\end{proof}

525	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:bad}
526	$P(\cA^c)\le Ce^{-cJ^2}$, uniformly in $f$.
527	\end{lemma}
528	
529	\begin{proof}
530	Each component $\partial^\iota\xi(x)=n^{-1/2}\W(\partial^\iota_xk_J(x,\cdot))$, $|\iota|=m$, is centred Gaussian. By (K3) its standard deviation is $\le C\bar\sigma_m$, where $\bar\sigma_m:=n^{-1/2}2^{J(d/2+m)}$, and its canonical metric is $\le C\bar\sigma_m2^J|x-x'|$. The Borell--TIS inequality at deviation $J\bar\sigma_m/2$ gives $P(\sup_D|\partial^\iota\xi|>J\bar\sigma_m)\le2e^{-cJ^2}$. A union bound over the finitely many $\iota$ with $1\le|\iota|\le3$ concludes the proof.
531	\end{proof}

533	\subsection{Assembly}
534	
535	\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}(ii)]
536	Let $r\le r_0$ (the minimum of the values required in Lemmas~\ref{lem:C4} and~\ref{lem:fields}) and $J\ge J_0$. On $\cA$ we have $\cA\subset\cB$, so \eqref{eq:star} applies. Clipping only decreases $|\tilde f-f|$, so Proposition~\ref{prop:bias} and Lemma~\ref{lem:rem} give
537	\[
538	\|\tilde f-f\|_2^2\le3|D|\big(CJ^22^{-J\alpha}\big)^2+3\|Z\|_2^2+3|D|\big(CJ^42^{-J(2\alpha-1)}\big)^2 .
539	\]
540	Off $\cA$, $|\tilde f-f|\le2r$ pointwise, so $\|\tilde f-f\|_2^2\le4r^2|D|$. Taking expectations, using Proposition~\ref{prop:var}, Lemma~\ref{lem:bad} and \eqref{eq:J},
541	\[
542	\E_f\|\tilde f-f\|_2^2\le CJ^42^{-2J\alpha}+C2^{-2J\alpha}+CJ^82^{-2J(2\alpha-1)}+Ce^{-cJ^2}\le CJ^42^{-2J\alpha}\le C(\log n)^4\rate,
543	\]
544	uniformly over $\Fc(\alpha,r)$. The finitely many $n$ with $J<J_0$ are covered by the trivial bound $4r^2|D|$. For non-integer $\alpha$, Lemma~\ref{lem:LP} and (C3) produce no logarithm. Then the bias is $\le C2^{-J\alpha}$, and the remaining powers of $J$ multiply terms of strictly smaller order. So the bound is $C\rate$.
545	\end{proof}
546	
547	Theorem~\ref{thm:main} follows from Sections~\ref{sec:lower} and~\ref{sec:upper}.

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{The variance: $\E\|Z\|^2_2\le Cn^{-1}2^{J(d+3)}\le C2^{-2J\alpha}$}{The variance}}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:var}
$\E\|Z\|^2_{L^2(D)}\le Cn^{-1}2^{J(d+3)}\le C2^{-2J\alpha}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
\emph{Representation.} Let $\mathcal D_y:=\bar f(y)\Delta_y+\nabla\bar f(y)\cdot\nabla_y$. By (G), $G_\xi(y)=n^{-1/2}\W(\mathcal D_yk_J(y,\cdot))$, and since Bochner integrals commute with $\W$,
\[
Z(x)=n^{-1/2}\W(h_x),\qquad h_x=\int_0^\infty w(s,x)\,\mathcal D_yk_J(y,\cdot)\big|_{y=\gamma_x(s)}\,ds,
\]
where $\gamma_x$ is the backward ray of $V_J$. Hence $\E Z(x)^2=n^{-1}\|h_x\|_2^2$.

\emph{Kernel bound.} Since $(2-\alpha)_+<1$, \eqref{eq:fbar} gives $\|\nabla\bar f\|_\infty\le CJ2^{J(2-\alpha)_+}\le C2^J$. With (K1) and (K2), $|\mathcal D_yk_J(y,z)|\le C2^{J(d+2)}\one\{|y-z|\le\delta_J\}$, where $\delta_J:=C_02^{-J}$. Let $\mu_x:=\int_0^\infty w(s,x)\,\delta_{\gamma_x(s)}\,ds$, a measure on $D$ of mass $\le 8/7$. Then
\[
|h_x(z)|\le C2^{J(d+2)}\mu_x(B(z,\delta_J)),\qquad
\|h_x\|_2^2\le C2^{2J(d+2)}\!\int\mu_x(B(z,\delta_J))^2dz\le C2^{2J(d+2)}\delta_J^d\!\int\mu_x(B(y,2\delta_J))\,\mu_x(dy).
\]
The last step is Fubini: $\int\mu(B(z,\delta))^2dz=\iint|B(y,\delta)\cap B(y',\delta)|\,\mu(dy)\mu(dy')$, and the intersection is empty unless $|y-y'|\le2\delta$.

\emph{Ray measure.} Let $x_J$ be the zero of $V_J$, $\rho=|\cdot-x_J|$, and $\rho_x=\rho(x)>0$. Let $\varrho(s)=\rho(\gamma_x(s))$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:geom}(4),(6), $w(s,x)\le(\varrho(s)/\rho_x)^\beta$ with $\beta=d(1-d\varepsilon)/(1+d\varepsilon)\ge7d/9>1$. Moreover $\varrho$ decreases strictly from $\rho_x$ to $0$, with $|\varrho'|\ge\nu\varrho$. Changing variables $t=\varrho(s)$, for every $\varphi\ge0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:M}
\int\varphi\,d\mu_x\le\frac1\nu\int_0^{\rho_x}\varphi(\gamma_x\text{ at radius }t)\,(t/\rho_x)^\beta\,\frac{dt}{t}.
\end{equation}

\emph{Small-ball mass.} If $|\gamma_x(s)-y|\le2\delta_J$, then $|\varrho(s)-\rho(y)|\le2\delta_J$. Hence, by \eqref{eq:M}, $m(y):=\mu_x(B(y,2\delta_J))$ satisfies
\[
m(y)\le C\delta_J\rho(y)^{\beta-1}\rho_x^{-\beta}\ \text{ if }\rho(y)\ge4\delta_J,\qquad m(y)\le C\min(1,\delta_J/\rho_x)^\beta\ \text{ if }\rho(y)<4\delta_J .
\]
(In the first case $t\in[\rho(y)/2,3\rho(y)/2]$ ranges over an interval of length $4\delta_J$; in the second $t\le\min(6\delta_J,\rho_x)$.)

\emph{Integration.} Apply \eqref{eq:M} once more, with $\varphi=m$. The part with $t\ge4\delta_J$ is
$\le C\delta_J\rho_x^{-2\beta}\int_0^{\rho_x}t^{2\beta-2}dt\le C\delta_J/\rho_x$, since $2\beta-1>0$.
The part with $t<4\delta_J$ is $\le C\min(1,\delta_J/\rho_x)^{2\beta}\le C\min(1,\delta_J/\rho_x)$. Trivially, $\int m\,d\mu_x\le\mu_x(D)^2\le4$. Hence $\int m\,d\mu_x\le C\min(1,\delta_J/\rho_x)$, and
\[
\|h_x\|_2^2\le C2^{J(d+4)}\min(1,2^{-J}/\rho_x)\le C2^{J(d+3)}|x-x_J|^{-1}.
\]
Since $\int_D|x-x_J|^{-1}dx\le C$ for $d\ge2$, Tonelli's theorem and \eqref{eq:J} give $\E\|Z\|_2^2\le Cn^{-1}2^{J(d+3)}\le C2^{-2J\alpha}$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The remainder and the bad event}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:rem}
On $\cA$, $\|T^{-1}_{\hat V}\dv(Z\nabla\xi)\|_\infty\le CJ^42^{-J(2\alpha-1)}$. This is $o(2^{-J\alpha})$ because $\alpha>1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
We use \eqref{eq:xi}, \eqref{eq:fbar}, $(2-\alpha)_+<1$ and $(3-\alpha)_+\le2$. First,
\[
\|G_\xi\|_\infty\le\|\bar f\|_\infty\|\Delta\xi\|_\infty+\|\nabla\bar f\|_\infty\|\nabla\xi\|_\infty\le CJ2^{-J(\alpha-1/2)}+CJ^22^{J(2-\alpha)_+-J(\alpha+1/2)}\le CJ^22^{-J(\alpha-1/2)} .
\]
Next, $\|\nabla G_\xi\|_\infty\le C(\|D^3\xi\|_\infty+\|\nabla\bar f\|_\infty\|D^2\xi\|_\infty+\|D^2\bar f\|_\infty\|\nabla\xi\|_\infty)\le CJ^32^{-J(\alpha-3/2)}$. Here each cross term has exponent $\le-(\alpha-3/2)$ because $\alpha\ge1$.

By Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b) and Lemma~\ref{lem:Treg}(d), with $\|D\dv V_J\|_\infty\le d\|D^2V_J\|_\infty\le CJ2^{J(2-\alpha)_+}$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:fields}(3), we get
$\|Z\|_\infty\le CJ^22^{-J(\alpha-1/2)}$ and
$\|\nabla Z\|_\infty\le C(\|\nabla G_\xi\|_\infty+\|G_\xi\|_\infty J2^{J(2-\alpha)_+})\le CJ^32^{-J(\alpha-3/2)}$.

\[
\|\dv(Z\nabla\xi)\|_\infty\le\|\nabla Z\|_\infty\|\nabla\xi\|_\infty+\|Z\|_\infty\|\Delta\xi\|_\infty\le CJ^42^{-J(2\alpha-1)}+CJ^32^{-J(2\alpha-1)}\le CJ^42^{-J(2\alpha-1)} .
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:T}(b) for $X=\hat V$ concludes the proof.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:bad}
$P(\cA^c)\le Ce^{-cJ^2}$, uniformly in $f$.

\begin{proof}
Each component $\partial^\iota\xi(x)=n^{-1/2}\W(\partial^\iota_xk_J(x,\cdot))$, $|\iota|=m$, is centred Gaussian. By (K3) its standard deviation is $\le C\bar\sigma_m$, where $\bar\sigma_m:=n^{-1/2}2^{J(d/2+m)}$, and its canonical metric is $\le C\bar\sigma_m2^J|x-x'|$. \end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}(ii)]

\[

\end{proof}
